title: Green-crowned brilliant hummingbirds feeding on lobster-claw flowers, Costa Rica
caption: Small birds, big impact
subtitle: Green-crowned brilliant hummingbirds in Costa Rica
description:
When it comes to aerial acrobatics, hummingbirds are in a league of their own. Found only in the Americas, these tiny birds can hover in place, fly backwards and beat their wings dozens of times per second. As they visit flowers in search of nectar, they also serve as important pollinators, helping sustain ecosystems from alpine meadows to tropical rainforests. Their shimmering plumage, remarkable agility and high-energy lifestyles make them some of the world's most fascinating birds.
Today's image shows green-crowned brilliant hummingbirds feeding on lobster-claw flowers in Costa Rica. Among Central America's larger hummingbird species, they are known for their iridescent emerald-green plumage and long, slightly curved bills, perfectly adapted for reaching deep into tubular blossoms. They inhabit humid forests from lowland regions to mountain slopes, where flowering plants provide a reliable source of nectar year-round. This feeding behaviour highlights the close relationship between rainforest plants and their pollinators, offering a glimpse into the interconnected web of life in tropical rainforests.

title: Lake Fyans, Grampians National Park, Victoria, Australia
caption: A reservoir of reflections
subtitle: Lake Fyans, Grampians National Park, Victoria, Australia
description:
At first glance, today's image looks more like a drowned woodland than a lake. Bare tree trunks emerge from the water, their reflections stretching across the surface as the Grampians glow in the distance. This is Lake Fyans, an artificial reservoir on the edge of the Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park in Victoria, Australia. Popular with boaters, anglers, sailors and water skiers, it offers a front-row seat to one of the country's most striking landscapes.
The mountains beyond the lake are part of the Grampians, a range shaped over hundreds of millions of years. Today, the region is known for its rugged sandstone peaks, dramatic lookouts, waterfalls and rich Aboriginal cultural heritage. Trails criss-cross the park, leading hikers to sweeping views and encounters with kangaroos, emus and other native birds. Lake Fyans captures that wild spirit in a single scene: flooded trees, open skies and an ever-changing backdrop of ancient mountains.

title: Old Town Hall, Bamberg, Germany
caption: Where history flows along the canal
subtitle: Old Town Hall, Bamberg, Germany
description:
Perched above the Regnitz River, the Old Town Hall is one of Bamberg's most iconic landmarks in Germany. According to local tradition, the building stands on an artificial island because the town's bishop refused to grant the citizens land for their town hall. In response, residents are said to have created their own site in the middle of the river, giving the structure its remarkable setting and enduring appeal.
The building combines elements of Gothic and Baroque architecture, while its colourful exterior is adorned with elaborate frescoes. A stone bridge connects the hall to both sides of the historic town, creating one of the most photographed scenes in Bavaria.
Today, the Old Town Hall remains a symbol of Bamberg's rich heritage and distinctive character. Surrounded by winding streets, historic buildings and riverside views, it offers a glimpse into centuries of local history and continues to captivate visitors from around the world.

title: Beech tree in a cereal field, East Meon, South Downs National Park, Hampshire, England
caption: Fields of gold
subtitle: Beech tree in a cereal field, Hampshire, England
description:
A beech tree stands alone amid golden fields near East Meon in Hampshire, providing a striking focal point in the rolling landscape of England's South Downs National Park. Agriculture has shaped these chalk hills for centuries, and farming remains an important part of the region today. The area's free-draining chalk soils support extensive arable farming, with wheat and barley among the most common crops. Throughout the summer, these crops ripen in the fields before harvest transforms the countryside into a patchwork of gold and stubble.
Early September coincides with the main harvest season, when rural communities begin celebrating the year's bounty. In villages such as East Meon, harvest traditions remain an enduring part of local life, reflecting the deep connection between the land and the people who work it. Framed by open skies and sweeping farmland, this solitary tree stands as a symbol of the South Downs' long agricultural heritage.

title: Gabit Keni Beach near Ankola, Karnataka, India
caption: Life on India's west coast
subtitle: Gabit Keni Beach near Ankola, Karnataka, India
description:
When people think of South India, they often picture spice trade routes, classical music, folk dances and a coastline that has connected India with the world for centuries. Follow that coastline west into Karnataka and you'll reach a quieter stop near Ankola: Gabit Keni Beach. Life here revolves around the Arabian Sea, with fishing boats setting out before dawn and returning with the day's catch.
The beach is named after the Gabit fishing community. It's an easy stop while exploring the Uttara Kannada district, especially alongside Gokarna, Karwar and the historic Mirjan Fort. Birdwatchers may spot coastal birds near the stream, while photographers often stop by during the softer light of early morning. Why not sample local cuisine? Fresh fish curries, squid fry and prawn dishes are popular at eateries around Ankola. Before you leave, make time for a fresh seafood meal—it may end up being as memorable as the beach itself.

title: The Roy Thomson Hall, Toronto, Ontario
caption: Plot twist pending
subtitle: 51st Toronto International Film Festival
description:
Ready for eleven days of movie mania? TIFF starts today, and Toronto is slipping into festival mode: coffee in one hand, screening schedule in the other. The event began in 1976 as the Festival of Festivals, giving Canadian audiences access to standout films from around the world. Fifty-one editions later, Roy Thomson Hall, along with other venues, is once again welcoming premieres, filmmakers and crowds hoping to catch the next big conversation before everyone else does.
This year's lineup features 293 films, with 'Being Heumann' by Siân Heder opening the festival and 'Villeneuve: The Rise of a Legend' by Yan Lanouette Turgeon bringing it to a close. Along the way, audiences can expect gala premieres, documentaries, shorts, industry events and late-night discussions that continue well beyond the theatre doors. One of the most entertaining TIFF traditions is the race for the People's Choice Award, where ordinary cinemagoers help decide which film leaves Toronto with the loudest buzz. So, which film gets your first popcorn at the festival?

title: Villefranche-sur-Mer, French Riviera, France
caption: Where the Mediterranean reigns supreme
subtitle: Villefranche-sur-Mer, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, France
description:
In September, the French Riviera is bathed in a softer light, and the Mediterranean landscape takes on fresher tones after the peak of summer. The hills are scented with Aleppo pine, rosemary and wild thyme. In the hinterland, centuries-old olive trees and hilltop villages tell a story shaped by Greek, Roman and Provençal influences.
Along the coastal trails, holm oaks and strawberry trees withstand the summer drought, while fig trees still offer an abundance of ripe fruit. In the bays of coastal towns such as Villefranche-sur-Mer, sailboats and yachts glide gracefully between sea and sky, while the red rocks of the Esterel Massif contrast strikingly with the deep green hues of the Mediterranean scrubland.
Around a secluded cove, the gentle song of the cicadas gradually gives way to a more peaceful atmosphere. The French Riviera offers far more than a postcard-perfect setting: it is a harmonious blend of nature, heritage and the art of living, where the Mediterranean reigns supreme.

title: California sea lions hunting a sardine bait ball, offshore Mexico, Pacific Ocean
caption: Masters of the surf and shore
description: A day at the beach is rarely quiet when California sea lions are around. With their booming barks, playful personalities and a knack for stealing the spotlight, these marine mammals know how to put on a show.
